_comment: Questions and checks for scripts/test-review.sh. Each level's `questions` object is sent to Jev verbatim; `checks` says how answers become findings. A noul check fires when its `applies` question (if any) is at least `applies_min` (default 0.5) and its `ok` answer, read as 1 - p when `invert` is set, is under `below`. A choice check fires when the chosen label is in `bad` at `confidence_min` or more. `verdict` is FAIL, CHECK (worth a look) or ENV (environment, never a failure). Thresholds come from calibration against tests/fixtures/test-review and the full suite with jev-1.13.0: a check keeps FAIL only where the bad case and the clean cases separate cleanly. Suite-level properties (a near-miss fixture exists, one FAIL branch hits the real tool, a stub drives the guard, PASS only on parsed data) are asked per changed function, where Jev sees every test for it, not per test. The negative-assertion trap is shellcheck SC2314/SC2315, checked exactly by the script.

side_effect_applies.instructions: The test asserts on a counter, flag or variable that the code under test mutates, such as _doctor_failures.

side_effect_direct.instructions: Every assertion on such a counter or flag follows a direct call of the helper, not a bats `run` call, which would discard the mutation in a subshell.

restates_const.instructions: The test only asserts that a pinned value (a tripwire count, a sha256, a version, a regex literal) equals what the source already says, without feeding the check a wrong value.

reads_source.instructions: The test's assertions read the production script's or patch's own source text instead of running it on a fixture.

level.instructions: What does this test actually verify?

criteria.syntax: Only that bash -n, shellcheck or node --check passes.
criteria.marker: Only that a patch marker, a file or a string is present.
criteria.behaviour: Runs the code on a fixture and asserts its output, exit status and resulting state.
criteria.real_tool: Runs against the real tool, real fixture bytes or the real bundle.

host_dependent.instructions: The test depends on the host: network access, a real gh or curl download, sudo, /dev/input or /dev/uinput, DISPLAY or WAYLAND_DISPLAY, or a HOME, XDG_* or _DOCTOR_* variable that setup() does not sandbox.

checks.title: Side effect asserted through `run`
checks.fix: Call the helper directly (not via `run`) before asserting the counter, as doctor.bats does.

checks.title: Test restates a pinned constant
checks.fix: If it guards behaviour, feed the check a wrong value (a moved count, a 63-char sha) and assert it is rejected, as installer-pin.bats does.

checks.title: Test greps the source instead of running it
checks.fix: Unless it pins deliberate structure, run the script or patch on a fixture and assert its output, exit status and resulting files.

checks.title: Syntax or marker check offered as behaviour
checks.question: level
checks.fix: bash -n, shellcheck, node --check and patch markers are the floor. If the change is behavioural, add a test that runs it on a fixture.

checks.title: Depends on the host
checks.fix: Sandbox HOME and XDG_* in setup(), unset ambient variables, and shim network tools on PATH.

drives_change.instructions: At least one of these tests runs the changed function (directly, or by running the script that defines it) through its changed branch and would see a different result if that branch were broken, rather than only calling it.

anchor_applies.instructions: The function matches its input with a grep, regex or string anchor.

near_miss_missing.instructions: None of these tests feeds the function an input one character or one call shape away from its anchor that must be rejected, such as a decoy site, a dropped ^ or a missing suffix.

stub_applies.instructions: These tests replace an external tool the function calls with a function stub or a PATH shim.

stub_only.instructions: No failure-branch test runs the real external tool on a real fixture; every failure these tests produce comes from a stub.

stub_never_fails.instructions: No test makes a stub return a failure shape that drives the function's guard to fire; every stub returns the happy path.

pass_applies.instructions: The function can print a [PASS] line.

pass_unparsed.instructions: The function can reach its [PASS] line with a value it never validated: empty, non-numeric where arithmetic follows, or a file type it does not handle.

checks.title: Changed branch not driven by any test
checks.fix: Add a test that takes the changed branch and asserts what it produces.

checks.title: Anchor without a near-miss fixture
checks.fix: Add a fixture one character or one call shape from the anchor that must not match, and confirm loosening the anchor turns a test red.

checks.title: Stub mirrors the production call
checks.fix: Run one FAIL-branch test against the real tool on a real fixture; keep the stub only for the un-fakeable case.

checks.title: Stubs never drive the guard to fire
checks.fix: Give the stub a failure shape and assert the guard fires (the [FAIL], the restore, the mismatch, the rejection).

checks.title: [PASS] on data never read
checks.fix: Guard empty and non-numeric values and every file type before the PASS branch, and add a test feeding each bad shape.

claims_uncommitted.instructions: The pull request description claims a verification (a manual run, a checked bundle, a mutation test, a shellcheck or node --check pass) that no test file in the list of changed files commits.

checks.title: Claimed verification not committed as a test
checks.fix: Codify the verification the description cites as a committed test.
